items.title: Baroreflex Activation Therapy in Patients With Resistant Hypertension: A Single-Center Real-World Analysis of Blood Pressure Response and Procedural Safety.
items.abstract: Baroreflex activation therapy (BAT) has emerged as a treatment option for patients with resistant hypertension; however, real-world data on blood pressure response and procedural safety of the second-generation Barostim Neo system remain limited. In this single-center retrospective study, 37 patients with resistant hypertension who underwent BAT implantation between 2013 and 2024 were analyzed. Changes in systolic office blood pressure (OBP) and 24 h ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) were assessed. Patients were classified as responders if any reduction in systolic blood pressure from baseline was observed. Periprocedural safety and procedural characteristics were also evaluated. In the overall cohort, no statistically significant reduction in systolic blood pressure was observed (ABP: 159 ± 27 to 157 ± 24 mmHg; OBP: 172 ± 19 to 165 ± 29 mmHg; both p > 0.05). However, a substantial proportion of patients showed a clinically meaningful response. Among responders, systolic ABP decreased significantly from 170 ± 24 to 141 ± 15 mmHg and systolic OBP from 178 ± 16 to 146 ± 17 mmHg (both p < 0.0001). A combined improvement in ABP and OBP was observed in 48% of patients with complete data. The mean implantation time was 74 min, and periprocedural complications occurred in 13.5% of cases. Generator replacement procedures were shorter and associated with a low rate of transient complications. In this real-world cohort, BAT using the Barostim Neo system appears to be a safe therapeutic option, although not all patients benefit. Among responders, BAT is associated with substantial and clinically relevant blood pressure reduction. Further prospective studies are needed to improve patient selection and evaluate long-term outcomes.

Impact of patient sex and dual antiplatelet therapy duration on 10-year mortality following percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents: A post-hoc analysis of the ISAR-SAFE trial.
items.abstract: Women are underrepresented in cardiovascular clinical trials and evidence regarding sex-specific long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains limited. To investigate the association between patient sex and duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with the 10-year prognosis of patients enrolled in the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled ISAR-SAFE trial. This post-hoc analysis included 1,871 patients from centers that participated in the ISAR-SAFE trial and agreed to collect 10-year follow-up data. In the ISAR-SAFE trial, a 6-month DAPT duration was compared with a 12-month DAPT regimen in patients treated with drug-eluting stents (DES). The primary endpoint of the present study was all-cause death at 10 years. Compared to men, women were older (69.0 ± 9.7 vs. 64.8 ± 10.4 years, P < 0.001), had lower body weight (72.1 ± 14.2 vs. 84.8 ± 13.5 Kg, P < 0.001) and a higher prevalence of arterial hypertension (93.2% vs. 89.3%, P = 0.031) and dyslipidemia (85.1% vs. 77.9%, P = 0.003). The 10-year mortality was 11.9% in women and 9.3% in men (hazard ratio [HR] 1.28 [95% confidence interval 0.91-1.81], P = 0.156). The 10-year mortality was 10.1% in the 6-month DAPT arm and 9.6% in the 12-month DAPT arm (HR 1.06 [0.79-1.42], P = 0.685). There was no significant interaction between sex and DAPT duration with respect to mortality. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality (adjusted HR per 1 year increase 1.08 [1.06-1.09]; P < 0.001). Among patients undergoing PCI with DES implantation, neither patient sex nor duration of DAPT regimen were independently associated with 10-year all-cause mortality after adjustment for relevant clinical covariates.

items.title: The ECMO-PoCS Score: Derivation and Internal Validation of an Implantation-Time Model for In-Hospital Mortality in Postcardiotomy Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
items.abstract: To derive and internally validate a mortality score (ECMO-PoCS) for use at venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) implantation for postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS), hypothesizing that a few implantation-time variables would discriminate in-hospital mortality better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II), Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II), or pre-ECMO lactate. Retrospective, single-center cohort study. Tertiary cardiac surgical center. A total of 149 consecutive adults receiving VA-ECMO for PCS (2007-2024), excluding 7 bridged directly to transplantation. None. Hospital mortality was 65.8% and 1-year survival 33.4%. A 4-variable logistic model (age, pre-ECMO lactate, peripheral artery disease [PAD], and any preoperative right ventricular [RV] dysfunction) was fitted in 133 complete cases; PAD (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 4.58; p = 0.022) and RV dysfunction (adjusted OR = 3.16; p = 0.020) were independently associated with mortality. In 130 patients with all comparators, ECMO-PoCS (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.715) discriminated better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) (0.583; DeLong p = 0.043) and lactate alone (0.601; p = 0.030) but not significantly better than APACHE II (0.610; p = 0.13); adding these variables to APACHE II increased its AUC to 0.727 (likelihood ratio p = 0.002). Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.687 and the shrinkage factor 0.82. A 0- to 5-point score defined low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (mortality 23.1%, 63.6%, and 86.0%, respectively; trend p < 0.001). ECMO-PoCS, based on 4 variables available at implantation, discriminated in-hospital mortality better than EuroSCORE II and lactate alone and added information to APACHE II. Internally validated only, it is intended for risk description, research stratification, and benchmarking, not for decisions to initiate or withdraw support, pending external validation.

items.title: A Wide pCR Divide: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy versus targeted therapy in resectable NSCLC.
No more surgery by default in dMMR/MSI-H colon cancer? From mandatory colectomy to response-adapted surgery.
items.abstract: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade has transformed localized mismatch repair-deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) colon cancer, producing unprecedented rates of major and complete pathological response. These results raise a question that until recently would have seemed premature: should colectomy remain mandatory in every complete responder? We argue that the next step is not routine omission of surgery, but prospective testing of response-adapted surgery. The central obstacle is no longer treatment efficacy, but reliable identification of a true complete response before resection. Unlike rectal cancer, colon cancer lacks a clinical complete response consensus framework, while residual nodal disease remains difficult to exclude. Endoscopy, imaging and circulating tumour DNA provide complementary information, but none is yet sufficient alone. Emerging trials are now directly testing non-operative strategies. Surgery should therefore remain standard outside clinical trials, while becoming a conditional intervention within carefully designed response-adapted studies.

Nanotechnology-enabled drug delivery for retinoblastoma: formulation strategies, ocular targeting and translational perspectives.
items.abstract: Retinoblastoma is an aggressive intraocular tumor in children, with a major underlying pathogenesis driven by mutations in the RB1 gene. Despite advances in management, current treatments, including systemic chemotherapy, focal therapies, radiotherapy, and enucleation, are limited by systemic toxicity, ocular complications, risk of secondary malignancies, and reduced efficacy in advanced disease. Additionally, poor drug penetration across ocular barriers and persistent vitreous seeding remain major therapeutic challenges. Novel drug delivery approaches such as liposomes, nanoparticles, and hydrogels have been used to achieve more localized treatment and reduce side effects. With the development of precision medicines, gene- and RNA-based therapies targeting genetic defects are promising approaches, but their targeting remains challenging. Immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as CAR-T cells, are being explored to restore antitumor immunity and overcome tumor immune escape. Therapeutic flexibility is enhanced by complementary natural products with anti-proliferative and epigenetic effects, while combination regimens, intravitreal chemotherapy, and biomarker-guided personalized therapy support clinical translation. Future clinical research should emphasize early diagnostic biomarkers and multimodal treatment combinations to maximize survival. This review focuses on nanotechnology-based ocular drug delivery, immunotherapeutic strategies, and emerging combination approaches in RB management, highlighting their translational potential, clinical progress, and remaining challenges for global implementation and accessibility. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language articles on nanotechnology-enabled ocular drug delivery, immunotherapy, and gene/RNA-based therapy for retinoblastoma.

The secular transition of pediatric diseases over 120 years: Insights from a historical exhibition at National Taiwan University.
items.abstract: The Department of Pediatrics at National Taiwan University Hospital (NTUH), established in 1906, has reached its 120th anniversary and has served as a cornerstone of pediatric medicine in Taiwan. As the nation's first pediatric department of Western medicine, it has played a leading role in advancing child health through innovations in clinical care, disease prevention strategies, and impactful research with national and global influence. Over the past century, its faculty has led initiatives that have profoundly shaped pediatric care, gaining recognition both locally and internationally. In 2021, we curated a special exhibition entitled "The Story of 115 Years: Exhibition of the Development and Progress of Pediatrics in Taiwan" at the Museum of Medical Humanities, National Taiwan University, a signature historic building that embodies the centennial legacy of medical education in Taiwan. This historical showcase aimed to inspire future healthcare professionals by tracing the transformative progress of pediatric medicine across different eras, highlighting how clinicians have responded to the evolving challenges posed by diverse disease patterns over time. The exhibition was organized into fourteen thematic sections highlighting major milestones in areas such as vaccine development, neonatal care, and novel treatment strategies. It served not only to honor the dedication and achievements of generations of pediatricians, but also to document their contributions to children's health, public health, and medical education in Taiwan. By illuminating the challenges faced and paths forged by previous generations, the exhibition highlighted the enduring legacy of the Pediatrics Department at National Taiwan University Hospital as a leader in pediatric innovation and care, fostering generations of pediatricians and researchers whose influence extends from Taiwan to the global pediatric community.

items.title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation strategy to achieve the functional cure for chronic hepatitis B? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Functional cure rate is low during continuous nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy, and therapy suspension has demonstrated interesting off-treatment responses. A systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate how stable, HBsAg positive-virally suppressed patients would respond to drug discontinuation in terms of HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, virological relapses, alanine-aminotransferases (ALT) flares, and necessity of therapy reintroduction were performed. Included studies were prospective, experimental and observational studies, including data on outcomes after NA discontinuation in HBV DNA negative patients with positive HBsAg, involving at least 20 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir, published from 2008 to February 2026, written in English language. A total of 28 papers (4495 patients) were included in the analysis, with low risk of bias: HBsAg clearance rate at 24, 48 and 96 weeks were of 3%, 8% and 11% (95% IC 1-8%, 4-15%, 7-15%) respectively, with low to moderate heterogeneity (I 2 =58.4%%, 66.5%, 47.3%); according to the HBeAg status at NA introduction, in those HBeAg negative the HBsAg clearance rates were 3%, 8% and 10% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively, while in those HBeAg positive 2.3 and 3.4% at 24 and 48 weeks, respectively. Overall a higher HBsAg clearance rate (39% at 96 weeks, 95% CI=10-78%, I 2 =83.3%) was described in patients with HBsAg <100 UI/ml at discontinuation. Treatment reintroduction due to virological and clinical relapse rates were 21%, 12%, and 17% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively. These results showed an overall low rate of HBsAg clearance after NA discontinuation, except for the patients with low HBsAg titers at this time. Thus, NA discontinuation must be balanced in the single case for the risk of virological and clinical relapses.

items.title: Reevaluation of the role of HBsAg testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility determination.
items.abstract: The utility of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility screening is uncertain in the era of concurrent hepatitis B virus (HBV) nucleic acid testing (NAT) and hepatitis B core total antibody (anti-HBc) screening. We performed an analysis of 300,112 deceased tissue and cornea donors. screened for eligibility between January 2021 and May 2026. Donors were screened for HBV NAT, HBsAg, and anti-HBc; results were analyzed to characterize HBV screening profiles and evaluate the incremental yield of HBsAg reactivity among donors with nonreactive NAT results. Overall, 97.02% of donors (n=291,180) had HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive results and 0.11% (n=318) of donors had HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-reactive results. In 0.57% of donors (n=1,697) HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-reactive results were obtained and 2.30% of donors (n=6,917) were HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive. Among HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive donors, 97.79% (n=6,764) were also anti-HBc-nonreactive. HBsAg testing identified 22.5 additional reactive screening results (per 1,000 donors) among donors without HBV NAT and anti-HBc reactivity. A subset of reactive HBsAg specimens were evaluated by supplemental confirmatory testing (n=1,131); only 17.28% were confirmed reactive. In this cohort, HBsAg testing identified potential donors for whom the biological significance of HBsAg reactivity remains uncertain, and current eligibility requirements result in donor exclusion.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.
items.abstract: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH. We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete. Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]). Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH. Merck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

items.title: Protein kinase C is a promising host target for anticoronaviral therapy in vitro and in vivo.
items.abstract: Host-directed antiviral strategies are urgently needed to counteract emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants. Protein kinase C (PKC) family members are involved in the replication of multiple viruses, but their role in coronavirus infections remains unclear. Building on our previous finding that pan-PKC inhibitors suppress SARS-CoV-2 replication in cultured cells, we herein investigated the underlying mechanism and evaluated the in vivo antiviral efficacy of PKC inhibitors in a mouse hepatitis virus (MHV)-infected mouse model. Go 6983, bisindolylmaleimide I, and sotrastaurin significantly reduced PKCα phosphorylation in Huh7 cells, whereas enzastaurin exhibited only a weak inhibitory effect. Importantly, siRNA-mediated knockdown of PKCα, δ, ε, and ζ substantially impaired SARS-CoV-2 replicon and viral trVLP replication, indicating that multiple PKC isoforms contribute to coronavirus replication. These inhibitors exhibited low cytotoxicity in murine 17Cl-1 cells and reduced MHV-induced cytopathic effects. In BALB/c mice, daily intraperitoneal administration of Go 6983 or bisindolylmaleimide I caused no body weight loss or pulmonary histopathological changes. Prophylactic treatment significantly suppressed lung viral RNA copies by 1-3 orders of magnitude, and alleviated virus-induced inflammation in both the lung and liver. Collectively, our results suggest that multiple PKC isoforms are potential host factors involved in coronavirus replication and PKC inhibitors exert potent antiviral and anti-inflammatory activity in vivo. These findings support the notion that PKC represents a promising host-directed antiviral target against coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2.

items.title: Hepatobiliary infections following hepatic tumor ablation in patients with prior biliary interventions: A propensity-matched analysis using the real-world global databank.
items.abstract: Hepatobiliary infections seriously complicate outcomes following liver tumor ablation. However, their association with prior hepatobiliary interventions remains inconclusive. This study aims to evaluate the impact of prior hepatobiliary interventions on the risk of hepatobiliary infections following liver tumor ablation. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network (2000-2025). Patients who underwent hepatic tumor ablation were identified and stratified according to prior ERCP or hepatobiliary surgery. The prevalence and risk factors of post-ablation hepatobiliary infections between patients, specifically focusing on liver abscesses and cholangitis were compared. Pre-specified subgroup analysis was performed, including age, cancer type, status of cirrhosis, and peri-procedural antibiotics. Of 14,307 enrolled patients, 632 well-paired patients were analyzed after propensity score matching (n = 316 in each group). Analytic results demonstrated that prior hepatobiliary interventions (including surgery and ERCP) significantly increased the risk of hepatobiliary infection (Hazard ratio: 3.50, 95% confidence interval: 2.40 - 5.11). This elevated risk persisted across all subgroups, regardless of age, cancer type, or cirrhosis status. Periprocedural antibiotics administration did not reduce infectious complications. Patients with prior hepatobiliary interventions had an increased risk of hepatobiliary infection after hepatic tumor ablation. Strategies to prevent infection in these patients are warranted.

items.title: Concentric-type immunoblotting coupled with LC-MS/MS for high-sensitivity analysis of exosomes secreted by sorafenib-stimulated hepatocellular carcinoma cells.
items.abstract: Exosomes exhibit excellent biocompatibility and low immunogenicity, making them attractive natural drug delivery carriers. Separation and quantitative detection of exosomal proteins and cellular signaling proteins are essential to decipher exosome biological functions. Traditional Western blotting (WB) is hampered by low sensitivity and limited detection range for low-abundance proteins. Concentric-type immunoblotting (CIB) integrates circular non-uniform gradient electric field with the molecular sieving effect of polyacrylamide gels to realize efficient separation and enrichment of proteins, effectively overcoming commonly false-negative issues in WB. Herein, exosomes secreted by sorafenib-stimulated hepatocellular carcinoma cells (SHCC-exo) were characterized by transmission electron microscope (TEM), nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) and CIB, verifying CIB as a high-sensitivity alternative to WB for protein separation and detection of low-abundance vesicular biomarkers in tumor-derived vesicles. LC-MS/MS confirmed that sorafenib-stimulated HCC cells actively encapsulate sorafenib, demonstrating successful fabrication of functional natural sorafenib-loaded exosomal delivery systems with intact bilayer membrane structure. Subsequent incubation of HCC cells with SHCC-exo was performed, and CIB was applied to sensitively quantify p38 and JNK proteins and their phosphorylated forms in the MAPK signaling pathway. The results indicated that SHCC-exo robustly induce HCC cell apoptosis via selective p38 activation, while the JNK signaling pathway showed no measurable activation under this specific drug treatment condition in vitro. This study demonstrates that concentric-type immunoblotting is capable of detecting diverse low-abundance disease biomarker proteins within tumor-derived exosomes, and represents a prospective analytical platform for tumor diagnosis, therapy-related molecular mechanism analysis and reliable quantification of phosphorylated proteins, offering promising application prospects for versatile protein analysis in related cancer biological research.

items.title: The IgG4ward! Foundation guidelines on the treatment of IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease is a chronic, immune-mediated, systemic condition that presents as tumour-like masses. Since publication of the last international consensus statement on the treatment of IgG4-related disease in 2015, the related literature has expanded considerably, with two phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trials published within the past 2 years. This foundation of evidence for treatment decisions justified new, dedicated treatment guidelines. 62 investigators-comprising 52 physicians, one medical reference librarian, eight patients, and one caregiver from 15 countries across six continents-were assembled to form a treatment guidelines group. The physicians had a broad range of specialties and patient representation spanned the full spectrum of organ involvement. The treatment guidelines group generated 183 candidate questions, which were consolidated into 40 final questions approved by the IgG4ward! Advisory Board. These questions formed the basis of a systematic literature search, led by a medical reference librarian, which informed the development of 28 treatment statements. Supporting evidence for each statement was independently graded using the 2011 Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence framework. The 52 physicians voted electronically on their level of agreement with each statement; consensus required more than 80% to agree or strongly agree with the statement, and was reached for 22 of the 28 statements. The evidence base reflects marked recent progress due to the publication of phase 3 clinical trials, although most statements still rely on low-level evidence. This effort provides cohesive, consensus-based guidelines from a geographically and professionally diverse group of experts in IgG4-related disease, reflecting the evolution in the field since 2015. Despite this progress, important knowledge gaps remain, and are highlighted to guide future research.

items.title: Stage-dependent management paradigms for MEN1-related Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: A vignette-based study by the ENETS MEN1 Task Force across 57 expert centers.
items.abstract: Management of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (ZES) in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) remains controversial, particularly in non-metastatic disease where the role of surgery is debated. In contrast, treatment of metastatic disease is guided by established systemic approaches. We aimed to evaluate stage-dependent clinical decision-making in MEN1-related ZES using standardized clinical vignettes across ENETS Centers of Excellence (CoEs). A questionnaire-based study using two clinical vignettes was conducted by the ENETS MEN1 Task Force across all 68 ENETS CoEs, with a predefined participation target of 70%. Additional non-ENETS expert centers were also invited. Dedicated multidisciplinary teams provided institutional consensus responses. Scenarios included non-metastatic disease, locally metastatic disease, and distant metastatic disease. Centers were stratified by volume using a cutoff of 30 MEN1 patients in active care. Data were analyzed descriptively, comparing management strategies between low- and high-volume centers. Fifty-seven centers participated (52 of 68 ENETS CoEs [76.5%] and 5 additional non-ENETS expert centers). All 57 centers completed the questionnaire in full. All cases received symptomatic therapy with proton pump inhibitors. In non-metastatic disease, management was heterogeneous, with 56.1% recommending surgery. Centre volume strongly influenced decisions (73.1% vs. 41.9% surgery in low- vs. high-volume centers, p = .018). Preferred surgical approaches included duodenotomy with regional lymphadenectomy (43.9%) and the Thompson procedure (left pancreatectomy, duodenal exploration with excision of tumors and node dissection, enucleation of pancreatic head lesions; 26.3%). In locally metastatic disease, surgical management increased to 78.9%, with a shift toward more extensive procedures including pancreaticoduodenectomy (35.1%). In distant metastatic disease, somatostatin analogues were the systemic therapy of choice (50.9%), followed by curative-intent surgery with pancreaticoduodenectomy or duodenotomy with regional lymphadenectomy combined with liver resection or thermal ablation of liver lesions (35.1%), while no other systemic treatments were selected by any center. A liver biopsy was recommended by 43.9% of centers. Management of MEN1-related ZES demonstrates stage-dependent convergence. In early disease, decision-making-particularly regarding surgical versus medical management-is highly variable and influenced by center experience, whereas advanced disease shows more consistent, guideline-aligned treatment patterns. The high participation rate across ENETS CoEs suggests that these findings are likely to be relevant to expert neuroendocrine tumor practice.

items.title: Impact of functional remnant liver volume on long-term outcomes after hepatectomy with bile duct resection for biliary tract cancer: Implications for a sequential portal and hepatic vein embolization strategy.
items.abstract: Functional future remnant liver volume (fFRLV) assessed using EOB-MRI predicts postoperative liver failure and severe complications after major hepatectomy. However, its impact on long-term outcomes after hepatectomy with bile duct resection for biliary tract cancer remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between fFRLV and long-term outcomes and assessed the oncological impact of sequential portal vein embolization (PVE) and hepatic vein embolization (HVE). Ninety-one patients who underwent hepatectomy with bile duct resection for biliary tract cancer between January 2014 and June 2025 were analyzes retrospectively. Patients were stratified using a preoperative fFRLV cutoff of 650 mL/m 2 . Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), recurrence-after survival and perioperative outcomes were compared. Patients with preoperative fFRLV ≥650 mL/m 2 had significantly better OS than those with lower fFRLV values (3-year OS: 72.3% vs. 31.8%, P = 0.0278); RFS was comparable between groups. Among 43 patients with recurrence, recurrence-after survival was significantly longer in the higher fFRLV group (P = 0.0270). Patients with higher fFRLV exhibited fewer severe postoperative complications and were more likely to receive and complete adjuvant chemotherapy. Twelve patients underwent sequential PVE/HVE. Despite significantly lower initial fFRLV, additional HVE did not adversely affect the oncological outcomes including OS and RFS. Preoperative fFRLV was associated with long-term survival after hepatectomy with bile duct resection for biliary tract cancer. Sequential PVE/HVE enabled curative resection in patients with severely insufficient remnant liver volume and function without compromising oncological outcomes. An fFRLV-guided surgical strategy incorporating PVE-HVE can optimize perioperative safety and long-term outcomes.
